source_notes: Lowland flooded rice requires consistent water depth.

preferred_value_or_description: Heavy clay, clay loam, or silty clay soils with low water permeability.
source_notes: Sandy soils are highly unsuitable due to excessive leaching of nutrients.

preferred_value_or_description: Basin flooding required to maintain standing water unless rainfall is exceptionally high.
source_notes: Water requirement ranges from 1200 mm to 2000 mm per crop cycle.

preferred_value_or_description: Optimal pH is 6.0 to 7.0.
source_notes: Slightly acidic to neutral soils preferred; poor salinity tolerance.

preferred_value_or_description: Optimal 20-30C; growth stops below 10C.
source_notes: Frost-sensitive; warm temperatures accelerate tasseling.

preferred_value_or_description: Evenly distributed rainfall of 500-800 mm during growing season.
source_name: ICAR - Indian Institute of Maize Research
source_notes: Waterlogging at seedling stage reduces yield drastically.

preferred_value_or_description: Deep, fertile loams or sandy loams with excellent drainage.
source_notes: Heavy clays cause root suffocation if saturated.

preferred_value_or_description: Supplemental irrigation during flowering and grain filling stages if rainfall is scarce.
source_notes: Drought during silking drastically impacts grain yields.

preferred_value_or_description: Optimal range 6.0-7.0; highly adaptable.
source_notes: Extremely high pH leads to iron chlorosis; acid soils limit vine vigor.

preferred_value_or_description: Optimal growing temperature is 25-32C.
source_notes: Frost below -2C kills green shoots; temperatures above 40C cause leaf scorch.

preferred_value_or_description: Requires dry ripening periods; optimal annual rainfall is 500-800 mm.
source_notes: Excessive rainfall during ripening causes berry splitting and fungal outbreaks.

preferred_value_or_description: Gravelly loams, sandy loams, or well-drained volcanic soils.
source_notes: Highly sensitive to waterlogging; clay soils are generally avoided unless tiled.

preferred_value_or_description: Regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) is preferred to improve grape quality.
source_notes: Over-irrigation leads to excessive vegetative growth and poor sugar development.
